newsitem.title: DUBAI: Gulf Arabs avoid mention of U.S. attacks on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Arabs avoid mention of U.S. attacks on Iraq.

text.p: Gulf Arab states on Sunday backed international efforts to ensure Iraqi compliance with U.N. resolutions, but made no direct mention of last week's missile attacks on Iraq by the United States, their key Western ally.
Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) members Saudi Arabia, United Arab Emirates, Bahrain, Oman, Kuwait and Qatar, issued a statement after a two-day meeting in Riyadh of their foreign ministers.
The GCC asserted "the importance of a unified political stand by the countries of the international coalition".

It renewed support "for all efforts and measures taken by the countries of the international coalition to ensure Iraq's adherence to total and precise implementation of all Security Council resolutions".

The statement did not directly refer to Tuesday's and Wednesday's U.S. missile attacks on southern Iraq, but said it was "greatly concerned" with "the grave developments in northern Iraq," an apparent reference to Baghdad's military support for one Kurdish militia group fighting another group.

It said the GCC "strongly condemns the interference of some neighbouring countries in northern Iraq and calls on these countries to immediately and completely halt the interference in Iraq's internal affairs".
The statement was apparently referring to reported Iranian support for one of the Kurdish groups in Iraq and Turkey's plans to set up a buffer zone in northern Iraq.
